explain: _volō_ ('I want') is followed by an infinitive: _bibere_ = 'to drink'. English 'I want to drink' becomes, almost word for word, 'to-drink I-want'. Either order is fine.
distractors: After _volō_ you need the infinitive _bibere_, not the I-form _bibō_.

explain: _edere_ is the infinitive of _edō_, with the same -ere ending as _bibere_.
Verbs like _dormiō_ have an infinitive in -īre: _dormīre_ (note the long ī).
Verbs like _ambulō_ have an infinitive in -āre: _ambulāre_ (long ā).
_legere_ is the infinitive of _legō_, with the same -ere ending as _edere_ and _bibere_.

en: I do not want to work.
explain: _nōlō_ is _nōn volō_ squeezed into one word, and it is the form Romans normally used. Like _volō_, it takes an infinitive. _nōn volō_ is also accepted.
distractors: Without the negative, this says 'I want to work'.
_dormīre_ = to sleep: 'I don't want to sleep'.

en: After the meal I want to drink.
explain: _post_ ('after') is followed by the accusative: _post cibum_ = after the food/meal. _ante_ ('before') works the same way.
distractors: _ante_ = before: 'Before the meal I want to drink'.
_post_ needs the accusative _cibum_, not the nominative _cibus_.
_edere_ = to eat: 'After the meal I want to eat'.

en: After the drink I want to walk.
explain: _potus_ ('a drink') is a fourth-declension noun. Its accusative singular is _potum_. _post_ takes the accusative.
distractors: _ante_ = before: 'Before the drink I want to walk'.
_dormīre_ = to sleep: 'After the drink I want to sleep'.

en: After sleep I want to eat.
distractors: _ante_ = before: 'Before sleep I want to eat'.
_bibere_ = to drink: 'After sleep I want to drink'.

en: After work I want to sleep.
explain: _labor_ (work) is a third-declension noun with the accusative _labōrem_. Don't confuse it with the verb _labōrō_ ('I work').
distractors: _labōrō_ is a verb ('I work'). After _post_ you need the noun _labōrem_.
_ante_ = before: 'Before work I want to sleep'.
_edere_ = to eat: 'After work I want to eat'.

en: Before the meal I want to wash.
explain: _ante_ ('before') takes the accusative, just like _post_. _lavāre_ means 'to wash' (here: to wash oneself).
distractors: _post_ = after: 'After the meal I want to wash'.
_bibere_ = to drink: 'Before the meal I want to drink'.
